Codex PASS lacked valid task or source evidence for every premise. PASS applies solely to the restricted A–E theorem for the entire declared class R. The current author argument and the complete supporting proofs n1–n3 establish the requested conclusions, including bounded and unbounded genuine potentials and the original capacity. Original unrestricted S02 remains incomplete; its historical INCONCLUSIVE report and invalid bindings 13–16 are not amended or inherited.

I checked the mathematical arguments independently. Source-read flags, symbolic-check verdicts, historical reviews and candidate metadata were not used as proof premises. All indispensable nonroutine foundations are expressly granted in task.problem, so premises=[]; the task passages below reproduce matching grants without reusing the historical external-premise indices. The [Xia–Zhang primary source](https://arxiv.org/html/2608.21053v1) and [Bedford–Taylor primary source](https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~ebedford/PapersForM655/BTNewCapacity.pdf) were also opened and checked. The Demailly URL did not reload, but the precise canonical-limit foundations used here are explicit task grants.

The smooth upper estimate is established with exactly the claimed constant. Dividing both Xia–Zhang’s background and operator by 2π preserves scalar potentials and positivity. Direct differentiation gives the matrix at every finite x, without importing its endpoint extension hypothesis for arbitrary smooth members of R. Its determinant and the normalized radial and fiber areas give MAω(V)=12AΔ dx dΩ dA, including semipositive matrices without division by the vertical coefficient. Periodic integration yields ∫EΔ=m″+μ(1−μ)−e″/2. The fiber mean m and vertical Dirichlet integral e are smooth invariant functions on the base; their radial derivatives vanish at both ends. Hence the nonnegative flux has integral one. Semipositivity gives Vxx≥−1; applying semiconvexity with displacement Vx proves |Vx|²≤−2V. Consequently ∫MAω(V)/(1+√(−2V))≤12, which gives precisely 12Q(W) and 12Q_T(W).

The bounded and unbounded passages cover all of R. Both local capacity comparisons are valid: the quadratic correction bounds global tests by local closed products, and sufficiently small gluing parameters produce genuine global tests in [−1,0]. Product domination follows by local regularization and positive mixed expansions. The compact group acts transitively by holomorphic ω-isometries; convolution is smooth, preserves positivity and rotational invariance, and converges in the original capacity by quasi-continuity, invariance and the stated Markov estimate. For uniformly bounded sequences, mixed positive trace measures are dominated by local capacity. Telescoping and bounded integration by parts therefore prove convergence in every degree. Expansion against the smooth remainder handles the nonclosed background without treating it as closed. Quasi-continuity and capacity domination justify continuous depth weights. Compatible strict truncations and monotone convergence then extend the budget, total estimate and tail estimate to every unbounded member of R.

The Borel estimate follows exactly by splitting at depth T: νW,u(A)≤W(0)(1+T)³Capω(A)+12Q_T(W). For continuity, fixed truncations preserve capacity convergence. The total variation error in replacing u by max(u,−K) is at most 24Q_{K−1}(W), for K>1. This includes the complete floor set {u≤−K}, including possible truncation mass on {u=−K}. Thus no boundary-level mass is silently discarded, and Q_T→0 proves weak continuity.

The faster-scale smooth family is globally admissible. The square estimate applies with all required parameters on the linear region and with κχ² on the initial region; χ=0 is checked separately. At ε=exp(−cη⁻³), the integrated defect is O(ℓ)+o(1), so a fixed sufficiently small c supplies the correction margins. The terminal cutoff error is smaller than background radial positivity. The correction removes the Schur-complement defect while controlling the angular coefficient, and its eventual constancy gives global smooth extension. The negative-end fiber mean and heat value bounds prove the stated canonical normalization and global depth bound. On the actual annuli, the completed square tends uniformly to one, the remaining negative terms are controlled, and their fiber area is 3t/2. The determinant density therefore gives mass at least Dη⁻¹ at depths between Aη⁻² and Bη⁻². Matching every sufficiently large t=Bη⁻² proves the necessary conditions for arbitrary decreasing weights, without regular-variation assumptions.

The single infinite-measure construction is also established. The controlled corrections provide uniform local derivative bounds away from w=0 and a global slope bound. The depth constant C* is fixed before scale selection; all recursive constraints can be met at arbitrarily large values of √t W(t). The local-submean propagation proof gives a uniform L¹ bound without BMP. Thus the decreasing series has a genuine canonical limit with current margin 3ω/4. On each selected core neighborhood the series converges smoothly, and the positive determinant inequality gives the actual local measure lower bound a_j³MAω(u_j). Normalization decreases depths and preserves the weighted lower bounds. The disjoint cores contribute at least one each, proving infinite weighted mass for one actual invariant potential.

The necessity arguments for C and D use actual measures. The cores approach H={z0=0}; local polar-capacity zero and decreasing compact-capacity continuity show that their original capacities tend to zero. In the bounded nonvanishing square-root regime, the controlled correction masses converge to m>0. The limit g is normalized and has local form m log|n|²−m log(1+|ζ|²)+constant near H. Its positive divisor current and the established smooth-part margins prove genuine global ω-psh admissibility and canonical value −∞ on H. Away from H, the heat exceptional sets shrink into tubes around the locally analytic section w=0. Their capacities vanish; together with correction convergence this proves actual capacity convergence uη→g. Uniform finite weighted masses give finite weak clusters. Portmanteau on shrinking closed neighborhoods forces positive cluster mass on H, whereas νW,g(H)=0.

The extra product calculation in n2 checks the floor levels explicitly. For large k, let g(x_k)=−k and μ_k=μ(x_k). The extended measure has total mass 6(1−m)² and gives no mass to {g=−k}. The bounded truncation has boundary mass 6[μ_k²−(μ_k−m)²] at x=x_k and floor-interior mass 6(1−μ_k²). Its entire floor level therefore has mass 6[1−(μ_k−m)²]. These identities follow from positive radial regularizations, the density 6d(A²), and bounded product convergence. They confirm that the truncation arguments retain genuine level mass.

Accordingly, A holds exactly when √t W(t) is bounded at infinity, for both universal individual finiteness and uniform total bounds. B–D hold exactly when √t W(t)→0. When the square-root quantity is unbounded, the single infinite measure obstructs a map into finite measures; this is not presented as a finite weak-cluster example. E follows from √t Wp,a(t)∼t^(1/2−p)(log t)^(−a): finiteness and uniform totals hold exactly for p>1/2 or p=1/2,a≥0; tails, uniform capacity absolute continuity and capacity-to-weak continuity hold exactly for p>1/2 or p=1/2,a>0.

The supporting P07 excerpt supplies only the valid local-submean and canonical compactness argument at the stated scope. The closed-elliptic diagnostic has consistent normalization and energy calculations and is not a Hopf counterexample or a dependency of sufficiency. The reproduced general damping proof follows from the granted depth estimates and the checked bounded-product passage. Xia–Zhang’s heat method and the known damping background receive the stated credit; no unrestricted reduction or priority conclusion follows.

The historical negative-slope expression must read sup[(Wη)x]₋, as the current article already does. At T=0 the total estimate supplies the tail bound; at T>0 one chooses 0<δ<T. These are harmless wording corrections. No substantial repair or unsettled essential check remains for restricted A–E.
